data.name: Adonijah
data.gender_notes: Adonijah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the Bible, Adonijah is a son of King David who attempted to seize the throne from his brother Solomon after David's death. The name 'Adonijah' is derived from the Hebrew 'adon', meaning 'lord' or 'god'. The name Adonijah carries the meaning “Lord, god, master” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Adonijah usually hope their child will grow to embody lord, god, master and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes a strong and determined leader, reminding us to trust in God's plan for our lives and to seek His guidance.
data.etymology: Adonijah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord, god, master.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adonijah total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: אדוניהו
in_hebrew.meaning: אדוני הוא אלוהים, אדוניהו משמעותו 'אדוני הוא האל'
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אדוניהו הוא שם פרטי עברי המורכב מ'אדון' שמשמעותו 'אדוני' ו'יהו' שמשמעותו 'הוא אלוהים'. השם מופיע בתנ'ך, במלכים א פרק 1, כאחד מבני דוד. אדוניהו היה בנו של דוד מלך ישראל ויחל בעקבות אביו. השם אדוניהו מבטא את האמונה באלוהים כ'אדון' וכמושיע.

in_greek.name: Αδωνιγιας
in_greek.meaning: Ο Κύριος είναι Θεός, Αδωνιγιας σημαίνει 'Ο Κύριος είναι Θεός'
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Αδωνιγιας είναι ένα προσωπικό όνομα ελληνικό που προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα. Το όνομα αποτελείται από το 'Αδών' που σημαίνει 'Κύριος' και το 'Ιγιας' που σημαίνει 'Θεός'. Ο Αδωνιγιας αναφέρεται στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη, στο 1 Βασιλέων κεφάλαιο 1, ως ένας από τους γιους του Δαβίδ. Το όνομα Αδωνιγιας εκφράζει την πίστη στον Θεό ως 'Κύριο' και σωτήρα.

in_latin.name: Adonijah
in_latin.meaning: Dominus est Deus, Adonijah significat 'Dominus est Deus'
in_latin.long_meaning: Adonijah est nomen proprium hebraicum quod componitur ex 'Adon' quod significat 'Dominus' et 'ijah' quod significat 'Deus'. Nomen Adonijah invenitur in Biblia, in 1 Regum capitulo 1, ut unus de filiis David. Adonijah fuit filius David regis Israel et successit patri suo. Nomen Adonijah exprimit fidem in Deum ut 'Dominum' et salvatorem.

in_english.name: Adonijah
in_english.meaning: The Lord is my God, Adonijah means my lord is God
in_english.long_meaning: Adonijah is a Hebrew name derived from 'Adon' meaning 'lord' and 'ijah' meaning 'God'. It appears in the Bible, 1 Kings 1:1-40, as one of King David's sons. Adonijah was a prince of Israel and attempted to succeed his father as king. The name signifies faith in God as the supreme Lord and savior. It symbolizes divine leadership and covenant relationship.

data.cultural_impact: Adonijah's name is a reminder of the power struggles and political maneuverings that have been a part of human history since biblical times. His story is a cautionary tale of the destructive consequences of personal ambition and lack of faith in God's plan.
data.spiritual_significance: Adonijah's name as a Christian given name serves as a reminder to always trust in God's plan for our lives rather than seeking power and control for ourselves. It serves as a call to have faith in God's sovereignty and to put our trust in Him alone. Additionally, it serves as a reminder to live with humility and servant leadership, avoiding the trap of self-aggrandizement and personal ambition.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Adonijah means "my lord" or "lord" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament, Adonijah was one of King David's sons who attempted to seize the throne. Despite his ambition, the name signifies a deep reverence and devotion to a higher power.

biblical_reference.note: Son of King David, attempted to become king of Israel

historical_references.reference: Adonijah was the fourth son of King David. He attempted to usurp the throne from Solomon, David's rightful heir, on the basis of his being the eldest living son. Adonijah's coup was foiled when Nathan the prophet and Bathsheba, David's wife, interceded on Solomon's behalf.

After Solomon's death, Adonijah made another attempt to seize the throne. He feasted his friends and invited Joab, the commander of the army, and Abiathar, the priest, who were both supporters. But God had given the throne to Solomon's son Rehoboam, and when the prophet Sheba came to confirm this, the assembly of Israel anointed Rehoboam as king instead of Adonijah.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Adonijah is seen as a classic and meaningful name in various modern contexts. It is often chosen as a baby name due to its biblical origins and associations with royalty. Adonijah is mentioned in the Bible as a son of King David and a potential successor to the throne. In terms of platforms, this name can be found on baby names websites as a popular choice for parents looking for strong and meaningful names for their children. On social media, Adonijah is sometimes used as a username or handle for accounts focused on royalty, succession, or biblical themes. Finally, Adonijah is also seen in historical dramas, particularly those set in ancient Israel or the Middle East, as a symbol of power, ambition, and royal lineage.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Adonijah from Dublin, Ireland embodies the meaning of Adonijah - "Lord, god, master". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
